articles.title: Court Rules on Ownership Dispute Over Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: A recent court ruling has clarified the ownership of Hopwood Hall, resolving a long-standing dispute. The decision is expected to have significant implications for the local community.
articles.content_html:
A court has ruled on the ownership of Hopwood Hall, a historic site in Rochdale, following a protracted legal dispute. The ruling has clarified the ownership status of the property, which has been a matter of contention for some time.

The decision is expected to have significant implications for the local community, particularly regarding the future use and preservation of Hopwood Hall. Local stakeholders have been keenly awaiting the outcome, as it may influence future development plans for the area.

While the specifics of the ruling have not been detailed in the source material, it is anticipated that the resolution will provide a clearer path forward for the management of the hall and its grounds.

Next steps for the parties involved have yet to be confirmed, but the ruling marks a pivotal moment in the ongoing discussions surrounding Hopwood Hall's future.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Court rules in ownership row over Hopwood Hall - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Court rules in ownership row over Hopwood Hall A court has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to pass ownership of Hopwood Hall to one of its descendants. Today marked the end of a two-day trial in the High Court in Manchester after Hopwood DePree took legal action against the council which ended an exclusivity agreement to sell the historic Grade II-listed hall to him. Following the decision, Mr DePree said: “This is of course incredibly disappointing and a huge blow to our community, our supporters around the world, as well as the UK’s charitable heritage rescue groups in general. “However, please know that my team and I are already determining our legal options and next steps. “We will be watching closely to keep an eye on Rochdale Borough Council’s efforts to save Hopwood Hall for the community, and restore it to its former glory.” Mr DePree is a descendant of the Hopwood family which build the manor house in the 1420s. The family owned the hall and surrounding land — which is now Hopwood Hall College — until 1922. The house was sold 20 years later. It was occupied by a variety of temporary residents, including the de la Salle Brothers, who ran it as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s. It had fallen into disrepair and was bought by Rochdale Council, which still owns the Grade II-listed property. READ MORE:Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026 Finalists Announced Mr DePree launched legal action after he spent seven years working with the council to carry out vital repairs on the dilapidated site with a view to purchasing it. In November, 2024, the council ended its exclusivity agreement with Mr DePree, and said it would explore other options because no “commercially viable” business model had been presented. Mr DePree and volunteers who worked on the hall have been barred from returning to the site since then. In the meantime, the council has spent £640,000 making the roof watertight. A council spokesperson said: “We are pleased with today’s judgement. It’s a shame that we had to endure a costly court battle to get to this point, as the time and money invested into this process could have been better spent on the hall itself. “We’re now focussed on moving forward. More than £1.6 million has been spent on the hall by ourselves and Historic England since 2017 and we will continue to invest in vital repairs to this historic building. “Feasibility studies have already been completed and options for Hopwood Hall’s long-term future will be considered in due course. “Whatever the future holds for Hopwood Hall, this building, once restored and refurbished, will be used for the benefit of the wider community of Middleton who rightly cherish it as an important part of Middleton’s rich and varied heritage.” SUPPORT THE ROCHDALE TIMES: FOLLOW US ON FACEBOOK Got a story? articles.title: Rochdale Council Moves Forward with Hopwood Hall Redevelopment After High Court Ruling
articles.excerpt: Following a High Court ruling, Rochdale Council has confirmed plans to redevelop Hopwood Hall, with an emphasis on community use, after ending an exclusivity agreement with Hopwood DePree.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced its commitment to the redevelopment of Hopwood Hall following a recent High Court ruling that upheld the council's decision to terminate an exclusivity agreement with American filmmaker Hopwood DePree. The ruling, delivered at Manchester Civil Justice Centre, concluded that the council acted lawfully when it ended the agreement, which had been in place since 2017.

The council leader, Neil Emmott, addressed the future of the historic building during a town hall meeting on October 15, stating that the council is focused on bringing Hopwood Hall back into use for the community. Emmott expressed openness to DePree's involvement, indicating that if he presents a viable plan, the council would consider it. However, he noted that the legal process is not yet concluded, as DePree has the option to appeal the decision by November 18, 2026, with a potential extension to November 28, 2026.

The High Court's decision came after DePree claimed he had a legally binding agreement to purchase the hall for £1, based on a planning approval granted in 2022. However, the court found that this approval did not trigger the option to purchase. The council has already invested over £1.6 million in repairs to the hall, and Emmott assured that any costs awarded to the council, amounting to £114,000, would be reinvested into the project.

As the situation develops, the council remains committed to the restoration and preservation of Hopwood Hall, which is seen as a valuable asset for the local community. Emmott reiterated that the council's focus is on securing the hall's long-term future, and the outcome of any potential appeal will be crucial in determining the next steps.

articles.title: Hopwood Hall to be Restored for Community Use Following Court Ruling
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council has confirmed plans to restore Hopwood Hall for community use after a recent High Court ruling. The council leader has expressed openness to proposals from the previous developer.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced that Hopwood Hall will be brought back into community use following a recent High Court ruling. The decision comes after a protracted legal battle involving the hall's previous developer, Hopwood DePree, who had claimed a right to purchase the historic building for £1.

The High Court ruled that the council acted lawfully when it ended an exclusivity agreement with DePree, which had been in place since 2017. The court found that a planning approval granted in 2022 did not trigger the option for DePree to buy the hall at the nominal fee. This ruling was delivered during a two-day trial at the Manchester Civil Justice Centre.

During a town hall meeting on October 15, council leader Neil Emmott addressed the future of Hopwood Hall, stating that the council is committed to restoring the building for community use. Although he did not specify what that use would entail, he expressed a willingness to consider any viable proposals from DePree, whose ancestral connections to the hall date back to the 1400s.

The council has indicated that the legal process may not be entirely concluded, as DePree retains the right to appeal the High Court's decision. Any application for permission to appeal must be submitted by November 18, 2026, with a potential extension to November 28, 2026.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Hopwood Hall ‘will be brought back into community use’ | Roch Valley Radio On Air Live now — track details aren't available right now Listen Live Watch Hopwood Hall ‘will be brought back into community use’ George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter October 17, 2026 | 10:56 AM Print The Grade-II listed Hopwood Hall in Middleton After a turbulent two years of battling over Hopwood Hall, Rochdale’s council leader says the ‘cherished’ historic building will be brought back into use. Council bosses were quizzed over the future of the Middleton site following a High Court battle where the town hall prevailed against Hopwood DePree. The two day trial in Manchester Civil Justice Centre ruled that the council was not acting unlawfully when it ended an exclusivity agreement with the American filmmaker. Mr DePree entered an option agreement with the council to restore the hall back in 2017, until that agreement was ended in October 2024. Since then, Mr DePree, who claims ancestral connections with the 1400s stately home,  has felt he had a legally binding agreement to purchase Hopwood Hall for £1. The High Court found that the ‘change of use’ planning approval was granted in 2022 wasn’t enough to trigger the option to purchase the hall for a ‘peppercorn fee’ – £1. In the first town hall meeting since the trial last month, council leader Neil Emmott was asked what the next steps were for the hall. Coun Emmott did not clarify a specific use for the future of the hall, but vowed to bring it back into use for the wider community. The council boss told the chamber on October 15 how his ‘door is always open’ to Hopwood DePree. Coun Emmott said if Mr DePree came back with a viable plan for the future of Hopwood Hall, the council would listen. In response to Coun Steve Potter’s question about the next steps for Hopwood Hall, Coun Emmott said: “The High Court’s judgment in relation to Hopwood Hall does not necessarily mark the end of the legal process. “Mr DePree has the right to seek permission to appeal the decision. The court has directed that any application for permission to appeal must be lodged by November 18, 2026, although there is scope for this deadline to be extended to November 28, 2026. “The council was awarded total costs of £114,000. I can confirm these monies will be reinvested into the project.  As part of any appeal process, Mr DePree would be required to make a payment into court of approximately £80,000 towards Rochdale council’s legal costs. “Should Mr DePree pursue an appeal, he would first need to obtain the court’s permission to proceed. This would require him to demonstrate that the proposed appeal has a real prospect of success or that there is another compelling reason for it to be heard. “Only Mr DePree and his legal advisers can determine whether an appeal is pursued. It is understandable that emotions remain strong within the local community, particularly among those volunteers who have dedicated considerable time and effort to the Hopwood Hall project. However, the council cannot move forward until the matter of the appeal is settled. “I can, though, assure the council and the people of Middleton that we remain focussed on the future of Hopwood Hall and the opportunities that now exist to secure its long-term restoration and preservation. More than £1.6m has already been spent on repairs to the hall by the council and Historic England. We will continue to invest in vital repairs to this historic building. “Whatever the future holds for Hopwood Hall, this building, once restored and refurbished, will be used for the benefit of the wider community of Middleton who rightly cherish it as an important part of Middleton’s rich and varied heritage.” Mr DePree has not mentioned whether his team will appeal the decision or not. The Hollywood man’s vision was to transform the hall into a wedding and hospitality venue, with a hotel ‘retreat’, gift shop and guided tours all part of the package. His team could regularly be seen working on the hall’s gardens and titivating the interior in the years since. The same community-led team were in attendance at both days of the trial and shared their frustration following the result in September. Speaking after the case, Mr DePree said: “Obviously I am incredibly disappointed. Not just me but the community of support around the world and the UK charitable groups as well. “I am already discussing with my legal team about the next steps. In the meantime I hope Rochdale council will be watching over Hopwood Hall because we will be keeping an eye on them. “We are not giving up. Hopwood Hall must be saved. In the two years we have been locked out the gardens have gone into wrack and ruin. I hope they will step up and save the hall. I still think the community group and I are the best people to take this forward. “I am getting messages from around the world with people offering money and support. It is a sad day but we will have to have a look at our options.” Add Roch Valley Radio as a preferred source on Google News to see more of our local reporting Add as a preferred source on Google Do you have a story for us?
